text:
elaine (product): ACME pinged asking for a "temporary reserve drawdown" option: let customers shrink their reserved pool briefly for maintenance/backups. Proposal they asked: up to 15% down for 3h windows, 2x/week, for a 6 month term in exchange for a 4% credit. Can we design this as a supported product feature?

mike (eng-platform): Clarify: when a tenant draws down, does that capacity immediately become available to other tenants (opportunistic fill) or is it held in a reserved bucket until the window ends?

elaine (product): They want opportunistic fill so we maintain utilization, but they require reclaimability at window end with a hard SLA.

lee (eng-sre): That combination is tricky. Opportunistic fill + guaranteed reclaim == preemption choreography. We need deterministic victim selection, admission controls, and a fallback path (e.g., warm standby) so reclaim doesn't cause long tail latency for co-tenants.

sara (sales): This is a frequent ask from finance-savvy customers. If we make it contractual with clear params, it'll sell. Need template terms: max drawdown, allowed schedule cadence, reclaim SLA, and a test/acceptance clause.

omar (finance): From a modeling POV: credit reduces unit revenue; but if utilization goes up we may net better. I'll run a conservative scenario: x customers adopt, avg commit, credit 4%, adoption ramp. Put numbers in RFC.

natalie (cs): Support impact: we must expose per-tenant telemetry (scheduled windows, last reclaim result, reclaim latency, credit ledger). Also support playbooks for failed reclaims and customer-visible incidents.

mike (eng-platform): Implementation sketch: add a Schedule object on reservations with drawdown blocks and `reclaim_grace_s`. Example config:```yaml
reservation: 2000_units
drawdown_windows:
  - weekdays: [Tue]
    start_time_utc: "03:00"
    duration_hours: 3
    max_pct: 15
    reclaim_grace_s: 600
```We'd need: scheduler scoring changes (opportunistic fill), a reclaim handshake that reserves reclaim tokens, and a fast-path to preempt if reclaim deadline approaches.

lee (eng-sre): +1. Add global and per-region concurrent-drawdown caps. Also a circuit breaker that auto-suspends drawdowns for tenants that repeatedly fail reclaim. Instrument: drawdown_active_gauge, reclaim_fail_count, reclaim_latency_p95, preempt_count_due_to_reclaim.

elainE (product): small typo? (not necessary)

elaine (product): For launch criteria propose: 1) reclaim success >= 99% in pilot; 2) reclaim p95 < 45s; 3) co-tenant tail latency increase < 7% p95; 4) billing and invoice preview validated; 5) support runbook + dashboards in place. Thoughts?

mike (eng-platform): Add: dry-run mode + simulation API so sales/CS can demo without moving real capacity. Also suggest incremental rollout: internal -> 2 pilot customers -> broader GA. Dev guess: 2 sprints prototyping + 2 sprints runtime + 1 sprint billing/UI + 1 support/docs.

omar (finance): Billing: prefer per-window crediting (easy reconciliation), but include a monthly summary for accounting. Need audit trail of successful vs failed reclaims to calculate partial credits if applicable.

sara (sales): Legal will want explicit SLA language and an escape clause if reclaiming fails and impacts production; also a clause for test/acceptance windows. I'll coordinate with legal and draft a templated addendum.

natalie (cs): Support test plan: simulate reclaim deadline missed, simulate reclaim with many concurrent drawdowns, and validate alert flow. Dashboard should show upcoming windows, recent reclaim outcomes, and credits earned.

mike (eng-platform): Implementation notes: reuse preemption stack but introduce a "soft-preempt" type that signals services to checkpoint state. Also we need fragmentation mitigation: coalescing drawdown returns into allocation sweeps to avoid tiny holes.

deploy-bot: Draft RFC available: https://rfc.internal/temporary-reserve-drawdown (WIP)

elaine (product): Action items: Mike -> own RFC & spec, Lee -> SRE runbook + circuit breaker design, Natalie -> support playbook + demo dashboard, Sara -> contract template, Omar -> financial model. Can we align on RFC + rough timeline by next Wed?

mike (eng-platform): I'll post RFC updates by Tue evening and include the milestone plan.

lee (eng-sre): I'll put together the limiter/circuit proposal and the metric list tomorrow.

natalie (cs): I'll build the demo script and wireframe dashboards.

sara (sales): I'll loop in legal and return a first draft next Mon.

omar (finance): I'll upload two scenarios (low adoption, high adoption) into the RFC for review.

elaine (product): Thanks team. Adding "temporary reserve drawdown pilot" to next roadmap review. Ping me if you want to be early reviewers. :rocket:
